lesson.text: Quick memory: in pseudocode, which word shows a value on the screen? (OUTPUT.) Today: writing programs as text, the way most programmers do.

Blocks snap together, so they cannot be joined wrongly. Text code is typed: quicker to write, easy to share and able to do far more, but every letter and sign must be right. Here is the same program both ways.
print shows something on the screen. Text goes in quote marks; numbers and sums do not. print("Hi") shows Hi, and print(3 + 4) works out the sum and shows 7.
A variable is set with one equals sign: score = 0 puts 0 in score, and score = score + 5 adds 5 to it. In code, = means becomes, not is the same as.
IF becomes if, and to compare two values you write ==. The line that starts a block ends with a colon. The lines inside it step in 4 spaces, as blocks inside an IF did.
REPEAT becomes for. for i in range(3): runs its stepped-in lines 3 times, and i counts 0, 1, 2: range starts at 0 and stops before 3.

A syntax error breaks the language's rules, so the program will not run. Worked example: line 2 says if coins = 5, but comparing needs ==. Also check the colons, pairs of brackets and quote marks, and the steps in.
Try it in the world: write the blocks REPEAT 4 TIMES, SAY Hello as text code on paper. Then check its colon, brackets, quote marks and step in. Next: lists.

exercises.prompt: Which line shows the word Hello on the screen?
exercises.hint: Text goes inside quote marks, inside print's brackets, and print is written in small letters.
exercises.explain: print("Hello"): the command in small letters, then brackets, and quote marks round the text.

exercises.hint: Go line by line and keep x's value on paper.
exercises.explain: x starts at 4, then 4 + 3 = 7, and print shows 7.

exercises.prompt: In text code, the line if score > 10 must end with a colon.
exercises.hint: What shows that a block starts?
exercises.explain: True: a line that starts a block (if, else, for, while, def) ends with a colon.

exercises.prompt: Match each block to its text code.
exercises.hint: SET and CHANGE use =, REPEAT becomes for, and SAY becomes print.
exercises.explain: SET score TO 0 is score = 0, CHANGE score BY 1 is score = score + 1, REPEAT 3 TIMES is a for loop over range(3), and SAY Hi is print("Hi").

exercises.hint: Are there quote marks inside the brackets?
exercises.explain: No quote marks, so the sum is worked out: it shows 5.

exercises.hint: Text in quote marks is shown just as it is.
exercises.explain: The quote marks make it text, so it shows 2 + 3, not the answer.

exercises.prompt: A misspelt command such as pritn("Hi") stops the program with an error.
exercises.hint: Does the computer know the word pritn?
exercises.explain: True: the computer does not know pritn, so it stops with a name error. Commands must be spelt exactly.

exercises.hint: Keep coins' value on paper after each line.
Is gems > 5 true? Only one stepped-in part runs.
exercises.explain: gems is 7 and 7 > 5 is true, so the if part runs and shows Lots; the else part is skipped.

exercises.prompt: The marked line stops the program. What is the mistake?
exercises.hint: Look at the very end of the marked line.
exercises.explain: for i in range(4) starts a block, so it must end with a colon: for i in range(4):

exercises.prompt: The marked line stops the program. What is the mistake?
exercises.hint: Text must start and end with the same mark.
choices: a line that should step in
exercises.explain: The text Well done! opens with a quote mark but never closes: print("Well done!")

exercises.prompt: How many Hops does this program show?
exercises.hint: range(5) counts 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. How many is that?
exercises.explain: range(5) gives 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4: five times round, so Hop is shown 5 times.

exercises.prompt: Why does x = 5 not compare x with 5?
exercises.hint: Which sign sets a value, and which one tests it?
exercises.explain: One = sets x to 5. To ask whether x is 5, write x == 5.

exercises.prompt: This program will not run. Which line has the mistake?
exercises.hint: Check the colons, pairs of brackets and quote marks, and which lines should step in.
exercises.explain: Line 3 is inside the for loop, so it must step in 4 spaces: the lines of a block step in.

exercises.hint: Write total after each time round the loop; i counts 0, 1, 2, 3.
exercises.explain: range(4) gives 0, 1, 2, 3, and total adds them: 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

exercises.hint: + joins text to text. Is name in quote marks?
exercises.explain: name holds Hoot, and + joins the texts: Hi and a space, then Hoot, so it shows Hi Hoot.

exercises.prompt: This program will not run. Which line has the mistake?
exercises.hint: Count the brackets on each line: every ( needs its ).
exercises.explain: Line 3 opens a bracket after print but never closes it: print("Eight!")

exercises.prompt: What is n when the program ends?
exercises.hint: Write n each time round the loop, and check the test before each round.
exercises.explain: n doubles while it is less than 10: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. 16 is not less than 10, so it stops at 16.
